rv.q: Reaching for a mic that hangs suspended above the stage, one tells of watching a fox decompose, another of a husband dying and another of his teenage daughter’s suicide. The stories are moving, even if links to Antigone’s own plight are somewhat tenuous.

Sophocles was a great storyteller and the material is all there for a fine and challenging evening. A small cast of seven are committed and earnestly perform with clarity and instinctive vigour. Running at 75 minutes without an interval gives a powerful and focused opportunity to get under the skin of the tragic and dramatic.

Having taken some time to digest the production, I will now attempt to convey to you just how extraordinary, biting and utterly devastating this show is. The original play Antigone traces its origins all the way back to Ancient Greece as an Athenian Tragedy written by Sophocles in 440 BC and premiered at that year’s Festival of Dionysus.
They are first glimpsed sitting together in a large white shell-like construct upstage (set by Alex Lownde ) which strikes a powerful picture as a background to the drama.
